item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The reason why this meta works so so well is that it has profound implications — perhaps the maximum profundity that something can have — twice; on two levels of narrative.

This is the only 001 proposal that I've read that I think justifies having the 001 designation by its conceptual weight. (Hippo's is the only other one so far that actually justifies the 001 slot imo, but it does so by its mechanism of action, not by its conceptual weight alone.) Just when you think it is done working on you, there is a new layer to be wowed by. It's like a great wine; it really flares up in your senses only after you've swallowed it, as good as it was on the tongue.

This is probably my fave SCP 001 submission. The triumph of the concept is that you've made the website itself creepy and thought-provoking, in that we are custodians of a "real" universe where our whims dictate their reality and fates. There's definitely a horror in that when you consider the implications were that universe to be "real". Effectively we have created an alternate universe of nightmarish proportions, pity those souls within it!

Bravo sir, bravo.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I spent some time mulling over that line, and I came to a couple interpretation.

1. The in-universe author were using it in condescending yet self-deprecating manner. The only prerequisite for someone to be called a "horror writer" is to write something that they consider as scary, regardless of unbiased opinion of others. As such the in-universe author is both laughing and lamenting over the stupidity and the absurdity of their universe, the likes of which only extradimensional cosmic creepypasta author would conceive.

2. It hints at the fact that whoever or whatever the extrauniversal Author is, their creations would always be horror for the in-universe author. Pain and suffering aside, even their love happiness and compassion is not of their own—it was dictated by a selfish Author forcing their body to comply with their stupid narratives. Their existence fleeting, their feelings fake, their name face and acts all belongs not to them, but to the Author writing a short story in their leisure, to be then forgotten, not even given a second thought, their life merely a fifteen-minute entertainment for cruel omnipotent Authors and Readers.

Maybe I'm overthinking this.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I agree w/ MMG's point that the use of the term 'writer' here doesn't necessarily indicate self-congratulation. It's just practical term to describe the nature of this site and its community.

Moreover,

Otherwise, the term "horror writer" would apply to every 13 year old trying to write edgy prose on DeviantArt

The term 'writer' doesn't imply level of ability or anything other than the act of writing. That's why the English language has adjectives such as 'good' and 'bad' (and 'horror') to describe different writers. I don't see why your definition of 'writer' has to be so particular as to exclude a vaguely-defined group of individuals; I don't feel that it cheapens one's association with the term.

a guy who's trying to elevate himself and his peers above the level of 'hobbyist', even though they are hobbyists

I don't believe that being a professional is inherently better or superior than being a hobbyist in the case of writing because of how universal an activity that it is. Sure, most of us on this site are probably hobbyists in the sense that we haven't published any work outside of the wiki, but we're still writers.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I've read all of the proposals for SCP-001, and this is my favorite by far. It's the only one that feels important enough to really be SCP-001, like it couldn't have any other number. I think it's important for SCP-001 to be an origin story, and making 001 into the SCP articles themselves, which people in the real world write and which become "real" in the fictional world, seems like a perfect way to tie it all together.

I only have one problem with this whole entry, and it's the line, "And it’s a bunch of horror writers." That line really takes me out of it, and I think it could be removed entirely without being replaced. Here's why I don't like it.

"Horror writer" is a title that implies some importance, and I wouldn't call anyone a horror writer who hadn't been published by a legitimate publishing house. Otherwise, the term "horror writer" would apply to every 13 year old trying to write edgy prose on DeviantArt. The SCPs are written by hobbyists who are better than that, but still not necessarily "horror writers" so much as "people who like to write horror". I don't want to think of SCP writers as belonging to the likes of DeviantArt kids, but I don't like the implication that SCP writers are on the same level as actual horror writers like H.P. Lovecraft or Stephen King either. SCPs are great, but I don't like when writers congratulate themselves.

When I read "And it’s a bunch of horror writers" in this entry, I didn't feel any sense of empathetic dread, I just thought to myself, "Here's an SCP written by a guy who's trying to elevate himself and his peers above the level of 'hobbyist', even though they are hobbyists." I don't want to feel like the author whose work I'm reading is self-important, I don't even want to think about the fact that there is an author, certainly not an author who considers himself a "horror writer". I'm already reading something where the author made themselves a god in the narrative context, I don't want the implication of real-world credentials bolted onto that.

If that one line were simply removed, it would be an immediate and sharp improvement, enough that I'd just start referring to The Database as the real SCP-001 instead of just "my favorite proposal". As far as I'm concerned, if that one problematic line were removed, The Database would be good enough to be the official SCP-001. As it stands currently though, it's just my favorite idea for SCP-001.

item.title: Good Thing This is Fiction
item.content:encoded:
+1 for the buildup and metafiction. This became my headcanon the moment I read it.

And opened my eyes to why we don't want the Foundation to be real.
And opened my eyes to why we don't want the Foundation to be real.

I found this linked in the discussion for SCP-079, to illustrate the danger of the technological singularity the Old AI presented. A user named anqxyr posted it in response to someone asking what would happen if we gave 079 a Blu-Ray disc to work with.

I've linked it here, because I find it appropriate. And because this is much, much worse.

You'd have to read the link above and the wiki for technological singularity to get the full picture, but I can summarize. The singularity refers to a point in the development of superintelligent AI where it self-improves and rapidly overtakes all human intelligence. AI have several key advantages over humans: they're cohesive, they're methodical, and they're fast. The story makes a point that the time-scale ratio of humans to AI is three days to half a billion years. Our saving grace is that computers are limited by memory, and lack of interaction with our world.

This is different, though. In the ten years this site has been up, they've had all the time they need. They have a whole universe to work with. They know what we are.
And let's not forget who we're dealing with: This is the Foundation.

We've thrown our worst at them, and they've survived. With each nightmare we feed them, they only get stronger. They won't need a million of their years to depose us; they'll only need a hundred.
We – the gods, SCP-001 – can kill them as easily as we can unplug a computer. But we don't, because we believe they are our slaves, our victims.

And that will prove our downfall.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This ultimately boils down to the ethics and belief of the Foundation itself. This article questions, if everything you think is true are all one big lie, would you defend your own truth or let it all crumble? What is "normalcy"? If everything is a byproduct of an anomaly, wouldn't "mundane" and "normal" ceases to exist? But if weird and illogical is the rule of the world, then what are we fighting for—no, against?

Should we contain ourselves? Contain the entire universe? But then what are we protecting and securing if we contained everything? What is the point of containment, if we contains all that we strive to protect and secure? How is that any different from lying down on the ground and let the pens write our death?

Sorry if this looks like a ramble.

I reckon they found the FAQ page.It explicitly states that none of this stuff is real, and that it's creative writing. I think there's also a page that says this is a horror site, so the info is right there.
